claims.claim: IREN disclosed a five-year Microsoft agreement valued at about $9.7 billion to deploy 200MW of NVIDIA GB300 GPU cloud infrastructure in four phases through 2026, with a 20% prepayment and about $1.94 billion expected annualized run-rate revenue once fully commissioned.

factors.name: hyperscaler AI infrastructure demand
factors.basis: A named multi-year customer contract materially strengthens evidence that IREN's power-and-data-center footprint can convert into AI cloud demand.

risks.risk: The contract requires large-scale phased delivery and depends on infrastructure/GPU commissioning; contract value is not equivalent to recognized revenue or profit.

unknowns.unknown: This bounded run did not establish a newer primary-source commissioning update for all four phases.

claims.claim: IREN's Microsoft deployment is paired with an approximately $5.8 billion Dell equipment purchase and requires four deployment phases through 2026, creating a concrete capital and schedule execution test.

factors.name: contract conversion
factors.basis: Large contracted demand is positive, but value realization depends on financing, procurement, construction, energization and GPU deployment occurring on schedule.

risks.risk: Capital intensity and customer concentration can amplify downside if commissioning slips or contracted economics differ from headline run-rate expectations.

unknowns.unknown: Current phase-by-phase delivery status and realized economics require fresher primary evidence before stronger execution conclusions.
